question: Which fixed-order unmaterialized physical families may be screened for the next fresh consecutive-query-triplet active-view test without selecting on future geometry or model outcomes?

selection.ranking: Use unchanged metadata candidate order. Exclude governed consumed targets, used reference families, the two explicit active-view predecessors, families with any already materialized required source file, and rescans without a second same-class door. Keep only the first target row from each distinct reference scan family and freeze the first six rows.

screening.order: Download and screen queue indices strictly in ascending order; stop at the first source-evaluable row. A failed row remains consumed as a source result and cannot be rescued or replaced within the queue.
screening.reference_memory: Require exactly three references under the unchanged positive-marginal plus maximum-angle vacancy rule.
screening.query_triplet: Require three consecutive source-admitted target frames, ranked by minimum visible target vertices, total visible vertices, minimum short-side fraction, minimum depth-visible ratio, then earlier frames.
screening.same_scene_negative: Require one source-admitted different-instance door or doorframe in the rescan.
screening.rgb_model_boundary: Pose and depth may be opened during source screening. RGB members and all models remain forbidden until the first evaluable row and its exact image cohort are separately frozen.

forbidden_after_freeze: reorder, add, drop or replace queue rows based on download size, source geometry, score margin, proposal recall, target IoU or action outcome
continue screening after the first evaluable row
open RGB or call a model during queue screening
change view rules, reference fill, triplet ranking, same-scene-negative requirement, trigger threshold, action or one-action budget
claim_boundary: This freezes only a metadata-selected ordered source queue before download, pose, depth, RGB and model access. It is not source evaluability, active-view confirmation, a deployable selector, exact-instance binding, portal ownership, affordance, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, benefit, reliability or safety.
